name: thumbcache_read
description: Read a Windows thumbnail or icon cache (thumbcache_*.db and iconcache_*.db of Windows Vista and later, the files that begin 'CMMM') and write every image it stores to a file: one file, or every such file under a directory. RULE: on a host whose files were encrypted or wiped, the thumbnail and icon caches may hold renderings made before; read them before calling a picture lost. Per cache file: format_version (0x14 Vista, 0x15 Windows 7, 0x1A, 0x1C and 0x1E Windows 8, 0x1F Windows 8.1, 0x20 Windows 10 and later; a version outside that list is refused, not guessed), cache_type with size_class_from_header (by the table of that version) beside size_class_from_name (a disagreement is a problem line), first_entry_offset and first_free_offset from the header, output_prefix (this tool's own name for the file: c001, c002, in the order read), the entries read and the bytes that are in no entry. THE READ BEGINS AT THE END OF THE HEADER (read_from_offset), whatever the header gives as the offset of its first entry: an entry that begins before that offset is read as an entry, marked before_first_entry_offset and counted (entries_before_first_entry_offset, a problem line and the status_basis say the header skips it), and bytes there that are neither an entry nor zero are counted like any others and make the file partial. Per entry, one row: file, entry (its number), offset, entry_size, entry_hash (16 hexadecimal digits), identifier (the entry's own name, which Windows writes as the hash; 128 characters shown), data_offset, data_size, declared_width and declared_height (Windows 8 and later), image_type by the image's first bytes (bmp, jpeg, png or unknown), image_width and image_height from a BMP or PNG header, the sha256 of the stored image, data_checksum and header_checksum (copied, NOT verified: checksums_verified is false), in_free_space (the entry lies past the header's first free byte: bytes of an earlier state of the cache, a candidate), before_first_entry_offset (only when true) and written (the file the image was copied to). An image is written under a name this tool makes (<output_prefix>-<the entry's number>-<its hash in hexadecimal>.<bmp|jpg|png|bin>; never the cache file's name or any other name from the evidence) in thumbcache_read-<id>/ under work/<your id>/ (in a job, under $OUT), and a file that is there is never replaced (the same bytes are named again, other bytes take the next free -n name). The images directory is the tool's own: where its name is a symbolic link or anything but a directory, and where $OUT of a job is not an existing directory, the call is refused before anything is read (nothing is written through a link, and $OUT is never created); only the entries list of the shared page (tool-output/) is placed by other code. EVERY LENGTH IS CHECKED: an entry whose parts do not fit its declared size is a row with an error and a problem line, and the next 'CMMM' is looked for; a file that ends inside an entry gives a row with truncated true; its image is written only when every byte of the image is in the file (data_bytes_present equals data_size: an entry whose declared size alone passes the end), and is otherwise not written; bytes that are neither an entry nor zero are counted and named (bytes_not_in_an_entry); each makes that file, and the answer, partial. AN ENTRY'S SLACK IS READ: an entry whose declared size is larger than its parts (header, identifier, padding, data) has the difference as slack_bytes, and the read goes on from the end of its parts, never from its declared end, so an inflated size hides nothing: an entry that begins in that slack is read like any other (listed, its image written), marked inside_entry_at (the offset of the entry whose size covers it), counted (entries_inside_another_entry) and said in a problem line and the status_basis; bytes there that are neither an entry nor zero are counted in bytes_not_in_an_entry (and slack_stretches_not_zero) and make the file partial; zeros there are the entry's own and change nothing; an entry whose declared size passes the end of the file while its parts are whole in it is read the same way to the end of the file. BOUNDS: max_entries (default 200,000), max_image_bytes (an image over it is hashed and not written; default 64 MiB), max_output_bytes (default 1 GiB; past it images are hashed and not written), 200 cache files of one directory, and the tool's own clock (100 s of the manifest's 120): each one reached is said and makes the status partial, with where the read stopped. status is complete only when every cache file found was read from the end of its header to its end and every image was written (with extract false: hashed), an entry found inside another's declared size being read and so not a reason for partial; with include_free false complete means read to the header's first free offset (read_to_offset) and says nothing of what lies past it, and the status_basis says so; failed when no file named is a cache. Not read, and answered as such: thumbcache_idx.db (the cache's index, 'IMMM') and IconCache.db (another format). Named by itself the index is failed; met in a directory beside the caches (every real Explorer directory holds one) it is listed in not_caches as not a cache this tool reads and does not make the answer partial, because no cache went unread. What an entry does NOT hold: the path of the item it was rendered for, and any time; tying a hash to a file needs the cache index or the Windows Search database, which this tool does not read, or a comparison by content. Only regular files are opened, without blocking and without following a link; a link is not followed. VERIFIED ON REAL DATA: the Windows 10 layout (0x20) against fourteen cache files of a real profile: the size class of every type number from 16 to custom_stream agreed with the file's name, and the 38 images written (37 BMP, 1 JPEG) are valid images by an independent reader; the layouts of 0x14 to 0x1F are from the published structures (thumbcache_viewer) and were run only against fixtures built from them. SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP end it with one JSON document (status failed, interrupted true, exit 128 plus the signal) and no temporary file; the images placed before a stop are whole files. A wrong-type or unknown argument is refused as JSON.

path.description: A thumbcache_*.db or iconcache_*.db file, or a directory holding them (a profile's AppData/Local/Microsoft/Windows/Explorer)

limit.description: Entry rows shown inline (default 100, 1 to 1000, an inline page size); every entry is read, and when there are more the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in all_results

extract.description: Write each stored image to a file (default true). false lists and hashes the entries and writes no image

include_free.description: Read the entries past the header's first free byte too, marked in_free_space (default true). false stops at that offset

max_entries.description: Entries read in one call (default 200000, 1 to 2000000); the rest are not read and the status is partial

max_image_bytes.description: The largest stored image written (default 67108864); a larger one is hashed, listed and not written

max_output_bytes.description: The image bytes written in one call (default 1073741824, at most 8589934592); past it images are hashed, listed and not written
